title: Google and Constellation Sign $4.3B Nuclear Deal for 890 MW

tickers.name: Alphabet Inc. Class A Common Stock

summary:
Constellation Energy will upgrade 11 nuclear reactors to provide electricity for Google's data centers under a new long term contract. The 20 year agreement aims to add 890 MW to the PJM grid and is backed by $4.3B in investment. Google also signed a separate 15 year supply deal covering an additional 2.7 GW of power, with the first uprate of capacity expected in 2028.

The pact makes Google the fourth major hyperscaler to secure energy from Constellation, following agreements with Microsoft, Meta and Amazon. Tech companies are increasingly contracting existing nuclear plants to secure carbon free power for AI data centers, as restarts and upgrades are faster than building new reactors. Google has also funded the restart of the Duane Arnold reactor in Iowa and capacity upgrades at two Southern Co. plants.

selectedTweets.text:
🇺🇸☢️ Big Tech is locking up America's nuclear power.

Bloomberg reports that Google is close to a $ 1B+, 
multi-year deal to buy nuclear power from Constellation for its US data centres. 

It could be announced as soon as this week.

It comes a week after Amazon signed a 20-year agreement with Constellation for 690 MW from Calvert Cliffs in Maryland. 

That includes 190 MW of new capacity from a plant upgrade, due between 2030 and 2032.

Google already has nuclear deals in place: one supporting the restart of NextEra's Duane Arnold reactor in Iowa and upgrades it's funding at two Southern Co. plants.

Tech companies are buying nuclear because speed matters. 

A new reactor takes a decade. 
An existing reactor runs around the clock, emits no carbon and is available now.
Upgrades and restarts are the quickest way to add new carbon-free capacity.

A power purchase agreement doesn't create electricity. Most of what Big Tech is signing for already exists, so every megawatt reserved for a data centre is a megawatt no longer available to the wider grid. 

The new supply is real but small. 

190 MW of uprates won't arrive until 2030 to 2032. 

Until then, the fight over existing reactors decides who pays more for power.

When AI companies outbid everyone for nuclear power, who gets left buying from gas plants?

Source: Bloomberg, Constellation

selectedTweets.text:
Google is reportedly nearing a $1bn+ nuclear power deal with Constellation ($CEG). MW, plant, exact tenor and delivery date remain undisclosed.

Prior deals: CEG’s Microsoft, Meta and Amazon nuclear contracts all run for 20 years. Microsoft restores 835 MW; Meta's uprate adds 30 MW; Amazon’s 690 MW includes 190 MW of new generation.

Included a capacity table assumes exactly $1bn of full electricity purchases, flat prices of $80–120/MWh, 95% nuclear capacity factor, full contracted volume throughout the term, no ramp and undiscounted payments.

MW = $1bn ÷ (years × 8,760 hours/year × 0.95 × $/MWh).

That gives ~100–150 MW over an assumed 10 years, or ~50–75 MW over an assumed 20 years. These are sensitivities; Google’s actual tenor and price are undisclosed.

As comparison despite different deal types: Amazon’s $3bn+ is plant investment; Microsoft’s ~$1.6bn is estimated restart capex.
